plain.li: Since I got hurt I watch where I put my feet, every stone and every root. I didn't know there were so many.
I walk round the loose ground now, even when it's the long way.
[child] I look at the ground the whole time now, so I don't fall again.

warm.li: I don't want to give anyone another fright. So I'm careful now, very careful.

blunt.li: I watch my step now. Once was enough.

cheerful.li: I've become an expert on the ground. I could tell you about every stone between here and the fields.

gloomy.li: The ground is out to get me. I'm not giving it another chance.

cold.li: Most falls come from not looking. I look now.

plain.li: I walked across the yard today without looking down once. I suppose I'm over it.

cheerful.li: I ran to supper today. Didn't even think about it.

cold.li: I've stopped watching every step. The habit wore off.

plain.li: I knock on the rock over my head before I swing at the face now. A sound roof rings; a bad one thuds.
Since the last time, I tap the ceiling before every shift. It takes a moment and it might save my neck.
[tribal] The old diggers sang to the stone before they cut it. I just knock on it, but it's the same idea.

warm.li: I tap the roof for everyone working near me, not just myself.

cheerful.li: Knock knock. Who's there? Not a rockfall, today.

gloomy.li: The mountain will come down on me one day. I'd like a warning first.

cold.li: A hollow ring means a loose roof. Testing costs seconds.

plain.li: I forgot to knock on the roof today, and nothing happened. Maybe I don't need to any more.

cold.li: I've stopped testing the roof. Most of it is sound.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: dries their boots by every fire

plain.li: After the weeks of wet feet, I dry my boots by every fire I pass. I won't go through that again.
My feet are still sore from the marsh. Every evening my boots go by the fire, and my socks with them.
[tribal] My foot wraps go by the fire every night now, and I change them every morning.

warm.li: I've started drying everyone's boots by the fire, not just mine. Nobody should get feet like mine.

blunt.li: Boots by the fire. Every night. No arguments.

cheerful.li: Warm, dry boots in the morning. I'd forgotten how good that feels.

gloomy.li: My feet will never be the same. At least they can be dry.

cold.li: Wet feet rot. Dry boots by the fire stop it.

plain.li: I left my boots by the door last night instead of the fire. My feet must have forgotten.

cheerful.li: My feet are fine now. Boots go wherever they like.

plain.li: After the fever I don't drink anything that hasn't been boiled first. I'm not going back to that bed.
I wash my hands before every meal now, and boil the water I drink. People think I'm odd. I'm alive.
[tribal] The healer said the sickness lives in still water. I boil all mine now.

warm.li: I boil a pot for anyone who wants it. Nobody else should have to go through that fever.

blunt.li: I boil my water now. Don't ask.

cheerful.li: Boiled water is my new favorite drink. It tastes like not being sick.

gloomy.li: Something in the water nearly killed me. I can't trust any of it now.

cold.li: Boiling kills most of what makes people ill. It's a small habit with a large return.

plain.li: I drank straight from the jug today without thinking. The fever must be a long way behind me.

cold.li: I've stopped boiling my water. The fear has passed.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: keeps an ember of the first fire

plain.li: I lit my first fire here from the embers of the first night's. I mean to keep it that way, every fire I light.
Every fire in this colony should come from the first one. I carry a coal from hearth to hearth.
[child] I'm the keeper of the first fire's ember now. I carry it in a little pot.

warm.li: That first fire brought us together. I want every fire here to remember it.

blunt.li: New fires get lit from the old one. That's the rule now.

cheerful.li: Our first fire is still burning, in a way. I made sure of it.

gloomy.li: If the first fire goes out for good, I think something here will go out with it.

cold.li: It's only fire. Still, the first one matters to people, and so it matters to me.

plain.li: I lit the stove with a match today and didn't think about the first fire until afterwards.

warm.li: Every fire here feels like ours now, wherever it was lit from.

plain.li: Late at night I find myself looking down the road toward the other colony. I don't know what I expect to see.
I keep a list of things to tell them when I see them next. It's getting long.

warm.li: I hope they're keeping warm over there. I think about them every night.

cheerful.li: I've started writing them letters in my head. They're very funny letters.

gloomy.li: Every night I wonder if we were right to split up.

cold.li: I think about the other colony more than is useful.

plain.li: I didn't look down the road last night. This place is home now, I think.

warm.li: I still miss them. But I sleep through the night again.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: sings a song from the strangers' fire

plain.li: The strangers sang a road song at their fire, and now I can't stop humming it.
I've picked up a song from the camp. I don't know half the words, so I make them up.
[child] The people at the camp taught me a song about a long road. I sing it everywhere.

warm.li: Their song stays with me. It's like they're still here, a little.

blunt.li: Got a song stuck in my head. Live with it.

cheerful.li: I learned a new song. Everyone's going to hear it until they learn it too.

gloomy.li: It's a sad song, about leaving. It fits.

cold.li: The tune is simple and good to work to.

plain.li: I tried to sing the road song today and couldn't remember how it went.

cheerful.li: I've got a new favorite song now. The road song had a good run.

plain.li: The sandflies came at dusk, and so did the fever. I'm indoors before the sun goes down now.
Three days of fever from one evening outside. I don't stay out after dark any more.

warm.li: I've been telling everyone to come in at dusk. Nobody should get what I got.

blunt.li: Dusk means inside. Learned that the hard way.

cheerful.li: Early nights for me from now on. I'll be the best rested person in the colony.

gloomy.li: The night belongs to the flies. They can have it.

cold.li: The flies come out after sunset. Being indoors then is simple prevention.

plain.li: I stayed out to watch the sunset tonight, and nothing bit me.

cold.li: I no longer mind being outside after dark.
